version.changelog: Initial release: batch deregister Consul service instances by ID or curl commands, supports dry-run, parallel execution, and ACL tokens.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: consul-deregister
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is a utility for deregistering Consul service instances via the Consul HTTP API. The Python script (scripts/deregister.py) uses the standard library's urllib to send PUT requests and includes features like dry-run mode, parallel execution, and ACL token support. While it includes a feature to parse and 'replay' curl commands, it does so via regex parsing rather than shell execution, avoiding command injection risks. No evidence of data exfiltration, persistence, or malicious intent was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements align with its stated purpose (deregistering Consul services via the HTTP API); it performs network requests to user-supplied agents and does not request unrelated credentials or install external software.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the behavior: the script dereferences Consul /v1/agent/service/deregister endpoints, supports service-id, parsing curl lines, agents-file, dry-run, and optional ACL token. No unrelated binaries, env vars, or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the included Python script and only to read an optional agents file; at runtime the script issues HTTP PUT requests to the provided agent addresses. It does not read arbitrary system files or undeclared environment variables. Note: SKILL.md examples use an absolute local path (/Users/shiheng/...) that may not match the runtime environment — that's a documentation mismatch, not a covert action. Also be aware that the script will send network requests to any hosts you provide.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction+script only and uses only Python standard library modules (urllib, concurrent.futures, re, json). Nothing is downloaded or extracted.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables or credentials are declared. The script accepts an optional --token parameter (X-Consul-Token) which is appropriate and proportional for ACL-protected Consul clusters.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no attempt to modify other skill or system configs. The skill runs only when invoked and does not request permanent presence or elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for removing Consul service registrations. Before installing or invoking: (1) review the script yourself (it's short and uses only stdlib), (2) prefer running with --dry-run first to verify the requests that would be sent, (3) do not pass ACL tokens unless needed and only use tokens scoped appropriately, (4) double-check the agent host list — the tool will issue HTTP PUTs to any addresses you supply, and (5) note the example path in SKILL.md is user-specific and should be adapted to your environment.
